blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Alpha diversity measures species richness and evenness within a single uniform habitat or local ecosystem.
Beta diversity quantifies the change or turnover of species between two distinct ecosystems along an environmental gradient.
Gamma diversity assesses the total species diversity across an entire region containing multiple ecosystems.
Biodiversity measurement relies on two core elements: species richness (number of species) and species evenness (relative abundance of each species).

blocks.content: Alpha diversity refers to the diversity of species within a particular ecosystem or defined habitat.

rows: Number of species within a single specific habitat
Rate of change or turnover in species composition between habitats
Overall species richness across large geographic landscapes

items: Competitive exams frequently ask to distinguish between Species Richness (count of species) and Species Evenness (closeness in numbers of each species).
R.H. Whittaker categorized biodiversity into Alpha, Beta, and Gamma levels in 1972.
A high Beta diversity indicates low similarity between communities and high environmental heterogeneity.
